source_snapshot.procedure: After topology inspection, inject `errType='uce'` at unresolved root-port coordinates.
source_snapshot.criteria: System stays normal; BMC/UEFI and fault light are all conditional.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; generic uncorrected/MCE text does not prove PCIe non-fatal severity.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: Requires target map, exact AER bit/policy and endpoint recovery.

old_problem: The token `uce` did not establish which AER bit was injected or whether current masks, severity and DPC policy classify it non-fatal; no mandatory oracle remained when all management indications were optional.
disposition_reason: The review-layer case can require an owner-signed AER bit and captured mask/severity/DPC pre-state rather than assigning semantics to `uce`. ED-03 makes slot mapping and policy runtime bindings; ED-16 prevents execution until the exact vendor contract and OOB recovery are present. Mandatory WHEA/AER, continued host operation and bounded endpoint/link recovery supply the missing oracle.
decision_basis: Read Reliability row 32, its DeepSeek data, historical record 2436, baseline row 33 context and next pending row 34.
Retained every PCIe slot and non-fatal UCE identity independently of CE/OCP/DPC variants.
Required proof of the actual AER bit and current severity before injection.
Made host continuity and endpoint recovery mandatory even when BMC/UEFI/LED are not applicable.
No injection or device recovery was performed.

test_case.purpose: For every approved physical PCIe slot, exercise one explicitly non-fatal AER bit and prove reporting plus bounded link/device recovery without host failure.
required_package: Endpoint workload and independent management-path assessment
Supported injector hash and exact AER-bit mapping
Captured AER masks/severity and DPC/firmware ownership policy
Windows WHEA/AER, recovery oracle and OOB restoration
test_case.test_command: Quiesce the mapped endpoint, capture AER mask/severity/DPC and link/driver baseline, and permit the FAE to invoke the signed UCE recipe for one root port only after it proves the selected bit is non-fatal. Correlate Cscript and Windows AER/WHEA, measure any recovery, verify host/endpoint service, collect applicable indicators, then restore state.
test_case.expected_result: Each required slot emits the designated uncorrectable non-fatal event, the host remains operational, the endpoint and link recover within the approved bound, optional platform indications match applicability and no residual fault remains.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires target identity, signed bit semantics, pre-state proof of non-fatal policy, exact WHEA/AER event, continued host service and bounded endpoint recovery. `uce` text alone, generic MCE output, fatal/DPC surprise, host reset or permanent link/device loss fails.
safety_gate: Dedicated or quiesced endpoint and independent OOB control.
Do not inject until severity/mask/DPC state proves non-fatal behavior.
One freshly mapped slot at a time; abort on wrong target or escalation.
No automatic reset or retry; preserve all register and recovery evidence.
expected_evidence: Signed slot/BDF/Cscript map and endpoint manifest
Package hash, selected bit and AER/DPC pre-state
Full injection plus Windows AER/WHEA transcript
Link/device recovery timing, host health and applicable platform indications
test_case.recovery: On escalation or failed endpoint recovery, stop the matrix, retain OOB/register evidence, use the approved device/platform recovery, restore policy/BIOS and demonstrate healthy service before any newly authorized run.

source_conflict.reason: The exact non-fatal bit and policy become signed execution inputs, while WHEA/AER and endpoint recovery form a mandatory acceptance core.

blocked.reason: No error-bit meaning is guessed; execution is safely gated by the vendor contract and captured policy.

pending.owner: PCIe platform owner and Intel FAE execute; engineer owns verdict.
pending.unlock_condition: Bind the exact target/bit/policy contract and recovery before injection.

project_authority: Project PCIe policy and supported injector contract determine non-fatal classification for each port.
